single_ablation.conclusion: The binary SMT peer-rejection condition was neither the alpha source nor a meaningful scarcity filter. Removing it changed no qualified signal or trade.

failure_classification.dominant_failure: A local range reclaim, opposite MSS, displacement/FVG and later retest did not establish durable failed-auction reversal. Seven of nine positions lost and the only material winner supplied effectively all positive PnL.

valid_components_preserved: separate completed displacement and later retest
pre-existing causal target registry with no measured move
one NautilusTrader account and global one-entry invariant
maximum planned and realized loss within the 3% NAV contract

research_process_correction.issue: The signal compiler used an exclusive end timestamp while the Nautilus calendar runner treated the same date as inclusive, producing an eight-day denominator although no signal traded on the extra day.
research_process_correction.future_contract: Future workflows declare a signal end-exclusive date and a separate Nautilus last-inclusive date so a random week contains exactly seven calendar days.

next_hypothesis: Replace binary leader/follower rejection with a cross-sectional common-order-flow factor. Route common-factor accepted sweeps to continuation and reserve reversal for idiosyncratic impact exhaustion; test the continuation branch first as an independent candidate.
